# Case-fact inventory — the drift surface

**Generated by `scripts/case-inventory.mjs`. Do not edit: the next run
overwrites it.** Re-run it after any change to a lesson or to `CASE.md`.

One question, answered repeatably: **how many references to a Cole household
fact can drift?** A figure inside the injected span cannot — it is overwritten
on the next inject and hash-guarded by `verify-case.mjs`. A figure matched by a
`verify-migration.mjs` check-20 pin cannot — a change to `CASE.md` that the
occurrence does not follow fails the check. Everything else can.

## Guard states

| State | What it means |
|---|---|
| `INJECTED` | Inside `<!-- CASE:BEGIN … -->` / `<!-- CASE:END … -->`. Cannot drift. |
| `PINNED` | Matched by a check-20 regex pin, which asserts it against `case-facts.json`. |
| `UNGUARDED` | Everything else. **This is the drift surface.** |

## The headline

| | Total | Quantitative | Qualitative |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `INJECTED` | 2737 | 2044 | 693 |
| `PINNED` | 8 | 8 | 0 |
| `UNGUARDED` | 169 | 45 | 124 |
| **TOTAL** | **2914** | **2097** | **817** |

**The number the unification rule moves is the quantitative `UNGUARDED` count:
`45`.** A qualitative reference — "Meg", "CPC", "Illinois" — is already
the target state under the rule *every quantitative case fact appears once,
injected from `CASE.md`; every other reference to it is qualitative*, so a
qualitative reference is not drift surface and removing one would be a loss.

## What this measurement declines to count

A fact whose surface form is not distinctive on its own — an age, a unit count,
a round percentage — carries a context test, and a match that fails it is
dropped. **The bias is deliberate and one-directional: this undercounts rather
than inventing drift surface.**

**1180 occurrence(s) declined.** `node scripts/case-inventory.mjs --misses` lists every one
with the text around it, so the undercount can be judged rather than trusted.
